description: Fetches data from a leaf route with optional facet filters, date range, frequency, and column selection. Use eia_describe_route first to discover valid facet IDs, facet values, column IDs, and frequency codes. Data values are strings in the response (EIA API returns all numeric values as strings, e.g. "9.13"); cast to DOUBLE in SQL when arithmetic is needed. Returns a preview inline and stages nothing by default — one upstream request, whatever total says. Pass stage: true to also page past the preview and stage the accumulated set as a DataCanvas table, then pass the returned dataset name to eia_dataframe_describe for its column names and eia_dataframe_query for SQL. Every dataset a tenant stages lands in the same canvas, so tables from different routes cross-join by name with nothing to thread between calls.

columns.description: Data column IDs to return (reduces payload). Defaults to all. IDs discoverable via eia_describe_route data_columns[].id. Every row also carries period and each facet ID whatever this lists, so naming those here is unnecessary and they are dropped from the request.

end.description: Period end, read the same way as start: a coarser end selects only its first period, so "2020" ends at 2020-01 at monthly — use "2020-12" to include the whole year. At hourly a date-only end covers its whole day.

filters.description: Facet filters keyed by facet ID (e.g. { "stateid": "TX", "sectorid": ["RES", "COM"] }). Use the facets[].id values returned by eia_describe_route as keys here. Every value travels in the request URI, which EIA caps at about 8 KB — a few hundred values across all filters; split a longer list across calls.

frequency.description: Aggregation frequency ID (e.g. "monthly", "annual"). Defaults to route default. Valid IDs from eia_describe_route.

length.description: Rows to fetch for the inline page (default 100; larger integers are clamped to 5000 with a notice). Every fetched row is used, but the response carries only as many as fit a 64,000-byte budget per surface — wide routes end the page early, said so in canvas_preview_note, with next_offset naming where to continue. With stage: true, staging is not bounded by this — it pages past the preview on its own.

offset.description: Row offset into the matching set (default 0). An offset at or beyond total returns zero rows.

route.description: Leaf route path (e.g. "electricity/retail-sales", "steo"). Discoverable via eia_browse_routes or eia_search_routes. Whitespace and slashes are normalized, then one complete leading v2 segment is removed: "/v2/electricity/retail-sales/" resolves to "electricity/retail-sales". Full URLs and /data suffixes are not normalized.

stage.description: Stage the matching rows as a DataCanvas table for SQL (default false). Off, the call makes one upstream request and returns the preview alone. On, the service pages past the preview up to EIA_CANVAS_MAX_ROWS and registers the accumulated rows, returning the handle in dataset — several extra upstream requests and seconds of latency on a large route, so turn it on when moving to analysis, not while exploring. Requires a canvas, which is on unless the server sets CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE=none; without one nothing is staged whatever this is set to.

start.description: Period start in the route date format (e.g. "2020-01" for monthly, "2020" for annual). Format from eia_describe_route. EIA reads a bound as the period of the effective frequency containing its first day, so a coarser bound selects that one period ("2020" is 2020-01 at monthly, "2020-Q4" is 2020-10). At local-hourly every bound needs its hour and UTC offset (YYYY-MM-DDTHH±HH, e.g. "2024-02-01T02-06").

name: eia_query_route

appliedColumns.description: Echo of the column projection as sent to EIA, when columns named at least one data column — period and facet IDs, which every row carries anyway, are not part of it.

appliedEnd.description: Echo of the end period as applied, when an end was provided.

appliedFilters.description: Facet filters applied to the query, when provided. Past 4,000 bytes the echo keeps the leading values and adds a "…" entry counting those not echoed per facet — every value was still applied.

appliedFrequency.description: Echo of the frequency as applied, when a frequency was provided.

appliedLength.description: Preview row count requested for this call.

appliedOffset.description: Row offset applied to the query — the cause when a page comes back empty.

appliedSort.description: Echo of the result ordering as applied, when a sort was provided — the ordering that decided which rows a capped stage holds.

appliedStart.description: Echo of the start period as applied, when a start was provided.

canvas_preview_note.description: Human-readable note, present whenever dataset is set or staging failed, and otherwise when total exceeds the inline rows. On a stage: true call it opens with the stage outcome: the staged row count and dataset name, naming eia_dataframe_describe for the staged column names (quoting one rename when staging renamed a column) and then eia_dataframe_query for SQL — or, when the canvas failed, that no dataframe was created (dataset is then absent), with the retry and offset paging. Next, where in the matching set the staged rows sit whenever the stage does not start at row 1, and when staging stopped short of total (the EIA_CANVAS_MAX_ROWS cap, the time limit of the call, or an upstream page that did not return) the offset to resume from; last, the inline page against total and next_offset — saying when the 64,000-byte response budget rather than length ended the page, or that a single row too large for the budget was withheld and offset + 1 steps past it — and, after a registered stage, that the inline rows page with stage left off, since another stage: true call stages a new table. Where staging was not requested it places the inline page against total and names stage: true and eia_dataframe_query as the way to get SQL access to the rest; where no canvas is configured at all, staging is unavailable, so it names offset paging and CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE=duckdb instead.

data.description: Inline rows: the first length rows from offset, ended early when the next whole row would push either response surface past the 64,000-byte budget. All numeric values are strings per the EIA API (e.g. "9.13"). Cast to DOUBLE in SQL for arithmetic: CAST(value AS DOUBLE). Per-column units appear as {col}-units fields inline in each row. Keys are dynamic column IDs from the EIA route.

items.description: A single data row with dynamic column keys.

dataset.description: df_<id> handle for the staged rows — eia_dataframe_describe lists its column names; eia_dataframe_query runs SQL over it (SELECT … FROM df_<id>). Present only when a stage: true call registered a table on a deployment with a canvas configured; absent otherwise, since nothing was staged. Every dataset a tenant stages shares one canvas, so handles from different routes join directly.

date_format.description: Period format for the returned data (e.g. "YYYY-MM").

effectiveRoute.description: The route path that was queried.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `upstream_invalid_response`: EIA returned an unusable response body or a missing route or data envelope. `upstream_unavailable`: EIA answered with a retryable HTTP service failure. `upstream_timeout`: EIA did not answer in time: one attempt passed 45 s, or the call passed its 56 s deadline across retries. Staging that runs out of time ends early instead, keeping the rows already staged. `route_not_found`: Route does not exist in the EIA taxonomy. `route_not_queryable`: Route is a category node with sub-routes, not a queryable leaf. `invalid_facet`: An unknown facet key was used in filters. `invalid_column`: An unknown data column ID was passed in columns. `invalid_frequency`: An unknown frequency code was passed. `invalid_sort`: A sort entry named a column the route does not sort by. `invalid_period`: start or end was not in a period format the route accepts, named a month, day, or hour that does not exist in the period shape its frequency reads exactly (YYYY-MM-DD at daily or weekly, YYYY-MM-DDTHH at hourly, YYYY-MM-DDTHH±HH at local-hourly), or lacked its UTC offset at local-hourly frequency. `uri_too_long`: The request URI passed the EIA limit of about 8 KB (HTTP 414) — typically a filter list of several hundred values. `no_data`: EIA returned no rows and start selects a later period than end at the effective frequency (the range is inverted). `rate_limited`: EIA rate limit hit (OVER_RATE_LIMIT). `upstream_unreachable`: EIA could not be reached (connection refused or reset, DNS failure) on the data request, the route metadata request, or the route-tree build. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

next_offset.description: Offset that continues right after the rows in data (offset + returned_count) — pass it as offset for the next page, with no gap or overlap. Present whenever rows remain past this page; absent on the last page.

notice.description: Composed guidance for empty results or an offset past total, unmatched filter values in complete cached vocabularies, year-only bounds on effective monthly YYYY-MM data, and requested/effective length when clamped. Submitted filters and date bounds are preserved. A row withheld by the response byte budget is explained in canvas_preview_note.

returnedCount.description: Rows in this response. When returnedCount < totalCount, continue at next_offset or stage the rest.

returned_count.description: Number of rows in data. When returned_count < total, continue at next_offset or stage the rest for SQL.

route.description: The canonical route path queried: whitespace/slashes normalized and one complete leading v2 segment removed. Reusable verbatim in a follow-up call.

total.description: Total matching rows in the EIA dataset for this query (may exceed returned rows when pagination or spillover applies).

totalCount.description: Total matching rows in the EIA dataset.

truncation_warning.description: Upstream advisories forwarded verbatim from EIA's warnings[], joined with '; ' when more than one applies. These describe the inline page — EIA's "incomplete return" entry fires whenever the requested length is under total, at any size — not a 5,000-row ceiling on this response. Absent when the response already accounts for the gap the advisory names (the staged table reaches the last row, notice explains the empty page, or canvas_preview_note places the inline page against total because nothing was staged).

title: Query EIA Route Data
